title: Best Indian Thrillers
description: Films that grip from frame one and don't let go — Indian cinema's tightest thrillers.
intro: A thriller lives or dies on its final act. These made it out alive.

entries.why_it_ranks: One of India's most brilliantly constructed thrillers. The tension comes not from action but from intelligence, family stakes and a protagonist constantly thinking several moves ahead.
A near-perfect black-comedy thriller full of reversals, unreliable perception and escalating danger. Ayushmann Khurrana and Tabu are exceptional.
One of Indian cinema's most effective serial-killer thrillers. The investigation, atmosphere and villain reveal are handled with relentless tension.
Vidya Balan anchors a tightly written mystery set in Kolkata, and the climax remains one of Hindi cinema's most satisfying thriller payoffs.
A bold psychological investigation where the protagonist himself becomes part of the mystery. Its final revelation completely changes how the film is viewed.
A dark investigative thriller driven by grief, alcoholism and a clever serial-murder pattern. Prithviraj gives one of his strongest performances.
A highly polished serial-killer procedural with excellent atmosphere, pacing and a strong investigative structure.
A compact, intelligent mystery that uses perspective and fragmented information extremely well. Remarkably controlled filmmaking.
A police investigation wrapped around grief and the supernatural. Aamir Khan, Rani Mukerji and Kareena Kapoor give the film emotional depth beyond the mystery.
Pawan Kumar turns an everyday traffic violation into a creepy, unpredictable mystery with a supernatural edge.
Funny, eccentric and surprisingly tense. Naveen Polishetty's detective character gives the genre a fresh personality.
Minimalist, tightly paced and driven almost entirely by performances and tension. Naseeruddin Shah and Anupam Kher are outstanding.
A stylish investigative thriller built around forensic science, serial killings and shifting suspicion.
Psychological horror and home-invasion thriller elements combine into a tense, inventive story led by Taapsee Pannu.
A missing-child mystery that continually questions whether the protagonist is being manipulated or losing touch with reality.
Often classified as psychological horror, but its mystery structure, investigation and gradual revelation make it equally effective as a thriller.
Sriram Raghavan delivers a stylish neo-noir about betrayal, greed and criminals turning against each other.
One of India's most inventive psychological thrillers. Reality, dreams and identity blur in a story that rewards repeat viewing.
A family discovers that a television serial appears to be predicting their lives. Simple premise, strong execution and steadily increasing dread.
Starts as a supernatural horror story and gradually reveals itself as something much more calculated and clever.
One of the rare sequels that expands the original thriller intelligently rather than simply repeating it.
A superb revenge thriller in which Urmila Matondkar's character transforms convincingly from victim to strategist.
A woman loses track of an entire day and slowly discovers that something dangerous happened during the missing period.
A police-gangster narrative structured around moral puzzles, shifting perspectives and the question of who is actually right.
A twist-heavy mystery where every new revelation changes the moral position of the characters.
